# Summarise a long PDF into 5 bullet points with Claude

Ever faced a huge PDF document and wished you could get the gist of it without reading every single page? This guide will show you exactly how to use Claude, an AI assistant, to summarise any PDF file into just five easy-to-read bullet points. By the end, you'll be able to quickly understand important documents for work, study, or personal life.

## Before you start
-   You'll need a free [Claude account](https://claude.ai/). If you don't have one, it only takes a few minutes to sign up with an email address or Google account.
-   Access to a computer or mobile device with internet.
-   A PDF file you want to summarise.
-   This guide assumes you are using the free version of Claude, which allows ample usage for this task.
-   **Rough total time:** 6 minutes.

## Step 1 — Get Ready for Claude
First, you need to open Claude in your web browser. Claude is an **AI assistant** – think of it like a very smart digital helper you can chat with, designed to understand your requests and provide helpful responses.

Open your web browser (like Chrome, Firefox, or Safari) and go to **claude.ai**. You'll see either a login screen or a chat interface if you're already logged in. If prompted, either sign in with your email and password or use a linked account like Google.

Once you’re successfully logged in, you'll see Claude's main chat interface, which usually has a clear area to type messages and a history of past conversations on the left.
You'll know it worked when you see the main Claude chat screen, ready for a new conversation.

## Step 2 — Start a Fresh Conversation
To get the best results, it’s always a good idea to start a new, clean conversation for each task. This ensures Claude focuses solely on your current request without being influenced by previous discussions.

Look for a button that says **"Start a new chat"** or **"New Chat"**. This is usually found in the top-left corner of the screen, often next to a Claude logo. Click on this button.

After clicking, the main chat area will clear, and you'll see a fresh, empty conversation window. A text box at the bottom will say something like "Message Claude…" or "Type your message here…". If it looks different, look for an icon like a plus symbol (+) or a speech bubble to begin a new discussion.

You'll know it worked when the chat panel is empty, ready for your first message.

## Step 3 — Attach Your PDF Document
Now it’s time to give Claude the document you want summarised. A **PDF** (Portable Document Format) is a common file type for documents, reports, and books, designed to look the same on any device.

In the message box at the bottom of the Claude chat window, look for an **attachment icon**. This usually looks like a **paperclip** or a **plus symbol (+)**. Click on this icon. A file explorer window will pop up from your computer. Navigate to where your PDF document is saved, select the PDF file, and then click **"Open"** or **"Choose"**.

You'll see the name of your PDF file appear above the message box, sometimes with a small preview or an "X" icon next to it, indicating it's ready to be sent. If you can't find the paperclip, try dragging and dropping your PDF file directly into the message box.
You'll know it worked when your PDF's filename appears within the Claude chat interface, ready for your instruction.

## Step 4 — Tell Claude What You Need
This is where you give Claude your **prompt** – which is simply the instruction you want it to follow. The clearer your prompt, the better Claude's response will be. You'll ask it to summarise the document into bullet points.

In the message box, where it says "Message Claude…", type your request. Make sure to specify the format (bullet points) and the number of points you want.

💬 Example: `Summarise this document into 5 key bullet points. Please use simple, plain English.`

Once you’ve typed your prompt, double-check it to make sure it's clear and asks for exactly what you want.
You'll know it worked when your text appears in the message box, alongside the attached PDF file, ready to be sent.

## Step 5 — Send Your Request to Claude
With your PDF attached and your prompt typed, the next step is to send it to Claude so it can start working its magic.

Look for the **send button**, which is typically on the right side of the message box. It often looks like a **paper aeroplane** icon or a **right-pointing arrow**. Click on this button to send both your PDF and your instruction to Claude.

Claude will then begin processing your request. You'll usually see a message like "Claude is thinking…" or "Generating response…" while it works. This might take a few moments, especially for longer documents. If the send button seems unresponsive, ensure you have both the PDF attached and text in the message box.
You'll know it worked when Claude starts typing out a response in the chat window, directly below your sent message and the attached PDF.

## Step 6 — Review and Refine Claude's Summary
Claude will now present you with the summary based on your prompt. It’s important to review this response to ensure it captures the essence of your document accurately.

Read through the 5 bullet points Claude has provided. Check if they cover the main ideas and if the language is indeed simple and plain as you requested. While Claude is very capable, it can sometimes **hallucinate** (confidently make up information that isn't in the document) or miss a subtle nuance, especially with very complex or highly technical texts.

If the summary isn't quite right, or if you'd like more detail on a specific point, you can ask Claude to refine it. For example, you could type: `Can you expand on the third bullet point?` or `Please rephrase the first point to be even simpler.`
You'll know it worked when Claude presents a clear list of 5 bullet points in response, ready for your review or further instructions.

## Common mistakes
-   **Forgetting to attach the PDF or sending a blank message:** Claude can only summarise what you provide. Always make sure the document name appears above the message box before you hit send. If you sent a blank message, simply attach the PDF and send your prompt in a new message.
-   **Using a vague prompt:** If you just say "Summarise this," Claude might give you a very general overview or a different format than you wanted. Be specific about the number of points and the desired language, like "Summarise into 5 bullet points, in simple English."
-   **Expecting perfect accuracy without review:** While Claude is powerful, it's an AI and not infallible. It might occasionally misinterpret information or omit crucial details. Always read the summary carefully and compare it to your understanding of the document, especially for critical information.

## What this means for you
-   **In everyday life:** Instead of spending hours reading lengthy terms and conditions, user manuals, or community notices, you can quickly get the essential information in a few bullet points, saving you time and effort.
-   **For your business or work:** Instantly summarise research papers, market reports, client proposals, or meeting minutes. This helps you and your team quickly grasp key takeaways, make faster decisions, and stay informed without getting bogged down in dense text.
-   **If you're just getting started:** The easiest first move is to try it with a PDF you've already read. This way, you can easily compare Claude's summary to your own understanding and see how well it works.

## Try it now
Find a PDF document on your computer – perhaps an old instruction manual, a news article you saved, or a school assignment. Head over to **claude.ai**, start a new chat, attach your document, and use the example prompt to get your first 5-point summary! You'll be amazed at how quickly you can distil information.
